The consumer confidence indicator measures households’ perceptions and expectations regarding the general economic situation in Belgium and their personal financial situation. It aims to summarise, in the form of a single indicator, the economic climate as perceived by households. The indicator is constructed from balances of answers to a set of questions in a monthly survey. The balance of opinion corresponds to the difference between the percentage of positive and negative responses, based on a scale of one to five ranging from “clearly positive” to “clearly negative”. The National Bank’s consumer confidence indicator (CCI) corr
approximately 1 850 households in Belgium. The sample is entirely renewed each month: participants are selected at random from the telephone directory, while ensuring a representative population in terms of geographical, social, demographic and income-related criteria. Interviews are conducted by telephone, via an external call centre, between the first and fifteenth days of each month. Prior to being contacted by telephone, selected households receive a letter explaining the purpose and confidential nature of the survey. The questionnaire focuses on households’ perceptions, estimates and expectations. Four main topics are covered: the gene
arithmetic mean of the balances of answers to four key questions relating to: the economic outlook in Belgium over the next twelve months; unemployment in Belgium over the next twelve months; the household’s financial situation over the next twelve months; the household’s capacity to save over the next twelve months. For the three “positive” questions (on the general economic outlook and the household’s financial situation and capacity to save), expectation of an improvement contributes positively to the indicator.
